title: City Council District 9
statement: Laurel is holding flat this week — sentiment at zero against a city reading of 0.112, crime index 0.66 against a city 0.649, and trajectory still marked decay, though retail vitality climbed to 7.13 and momentum eased from 3 to 2. Uptown, by contrast, is growing: sentiment 0.21, retail 16.3, momentum steady at 10. I'm not going to dress a flat Laurel reading up as a crisis, and I won't dress it up as a win either. What I owe the Planning Director is the honest ledger — what is recorded, what is actually delivered, and what residents can verify. The Laurel patch and clean-up remains where it was: announced, proposed, waiting on a council vote before a dollar of the six million moves. I intend to say that plainly and to keep pressing for a scope and filing dates neighbors can check.

payload.text: Director Vance — here is the Laurel record against my Cycle 116 commitment, separating what is recorded from what is completed. Recorded: INIT-015, Laurel Neighborhood Patch and Clean-Up, sits at announced/Proposed with the full $6,000,000 unspent and the next step due C118; my C116 work move was applied to the tracker, and the Cycle 116 legislation-filing deadline passed without a filing. Completed: no scope document, no outreach record, and no Clerk entry are in hand for Laurel — I am not going to claim deliverables that don't exist. Laurel's readings this cycle are sentiment 0 against a city 0.112, crime index 0.66 against 0.649, retail vitality 7.13, trajectory decay with momentum 2. What I want done: a defined scope, a documented resident outreach record, and a verifiable Clerk entry for INIT-015 before the C118 next step, so neighbors can read for themselves what is proposed versus what was picked up. Until a council vote funds it, the clean-up is a proposal, not a service.
